abbey.en: part of a street and theatre name in Dublin
abbey.zh: Abbey Street／Abbey Theatre（都柏林街名／劇院名）

about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

accommodate.en: to have space for; to hold
accommodate.ex: The hall can accommodate three hundred guests.

example.en: The new hall can accommodate a full orchestra.
example.zh: 新的大廳可以容納一整支管弦樂團。

note.meaning: 容納、提供空間給（人或活動）；也可指迎合需要。
note.usage: 常接人數或活動：accommodate 200 people；被動 can be accommodated。

noteEn.meaning: to have enough space for people or activities.
noteEn.usage: Often used with a number: accommodate 200 people.

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva sala puede albergar una orquesta completa.
noteEs.meaning: tener espacio para personas o actividades.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir con un número: accommodate 200 people.

noteHi.exampleTr: नया हॉल पूरे ऑर्केस्ट्रा को समा सकता है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ या लोगों के लिए जगह होना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर संख्या के साथ: accommodate 200 people।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新しいホールはオーケストラ全体を収容できる。
noteJa.meaning: 人や活動のための空間を持つ；収容する。
noteJa.usage: accommodate 200 people のように人数と使うことが多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 홀은 오케스트라 전체를 수용할 수 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 사람이나 활동을 위한 공간이 있다; 수용하다.

acoustics.en: how well sound can be heard in a room
acoustics.ex: The new concert hall has excellent acoustics.

example.en: The old church has wonderful acoustics for choirs.
example.zh: 這座老教堂的音響效果非常適合合唱團。

note.meaning: 音響效果：房間或建築中聲音傳播與聽起來的品質。
note.usage: 指建築音響時作複數用，動詞用 are；作「聲學」學科時用單數。

noteEn.meaning: how well sound can be heard in a room or building.
noteEn.usage: For rooms it is plural: the acoustics are good.

noteEs.exampleTr: La vieja iglesia tiene una acústica maravillosa para coros.
noteEs.meaning: la calidad del sonido en una sala o edificio.
noteEs.usage: Para salas se usa en plural (are).

noteHi.exampleTr: पुराने चर्च की ध्वनिकी गायक-मंडलियों के लिए शानदार है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी कमरे में आवाज़ कितनी अच्छी सुनाई देती है, यह गुण।
noteHi.usage: कमरे के लिए बहुवचन (are) के साथ प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その古い教会は合唱団にとってすばらしい音響を持っている。
noteJa.meaning: 部屋や建物での音の響き具合。
noteJa.usage: 部屋の音響の意味では複数扱い（are）。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 오래된 교회는 합창단에 훌륭한 음향을 갖추고 있다.
noteKo.usage: 방의 음향을 말할 때는 복수 취급(are)한다.

acquired.ex: The museum acquired a rare painting last year.

example.en: The university has acquired a new building for its music school.
example.zh: 這所大學為音樂學院購得了一棟新建築。

note.meaning: 取得、購得（尤指以購買方式獲得資產、建築或公司）。
note.usage: 比 buy 正式，常用於新聞與商業；名詞為 acquisition。

noteEn.meaning: to get something, often by buying it.
noteEn.usage: More formal than buy; the noun is acquisition.

noteEs.exampleTr: La universidad ha adquirido un nuevo edificio para su escuela de música.
noteEs.meaning: obtener algo, sobre todo comprando un edificio o una empresa.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que buy; el sustantivo es acquisition.

noteHi.exampleTr: विश्वविद्यालय ने अपने संगीत विद्यालय के लिए एक नई इमारत खरीदी है।
noteHi.meaning: कुछ (जैसे इमारत या कंपनी) खरीदकर प्राप्त करना।
noteHi.usage: buy से अधिक औपचारिक; संज्ञा acquisition है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その大学は音楽学部のために新しい建物を取得した。
noteJa.meaning: （建物や会社などを）購入して手に入れる。
noteJa.usage: buy より改まった語で、名詞は acquisition。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 대학은 음악 학부를 위해 새 건물을 매입했다.
noteKo.usage: buy보다 격식 있는 말이며 명사는 acquisition이다.

acquisition.ex: The acquisition of the farm took six months.

adequate.ex: Make sure you get adequate sleep before exams.

almost.ex: The train was almost empty at midnight.

amenity.en: a useful public building or service
amenity.ex: A library is an important amenity for any town.

anticipates.ex: We anticipate a busy summer at the café.

example.en: The theatre anticipates large crowds on opening night.
example.zh: 劇院預期首演之夜會有大批觀眾。

note.meaning: 預期、預料（某事會發生），並常為此做準備。
note.usage: 接名詞、動名詞或 that 子句；不接 to do。比 expect 正式。

noteEn.meaning: to expect that something will happen.
noteEn.usage: Use it with a noun, -ing or a that clause; more formal than expect.

noteEs.exampleTr: El teatro prevé grandes multitudes en la noche del estreno.
noteEs.meaning: esperar que algo ocurra, a menudo preparándose.
noteEs.usage: Va con sustantivo, -ing o that; más formal que expect.

noteHi.exampleTr: थिएटर को पहली रात भारी भीड़ की उम्मीद है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात के होने की उम्मीद करना।
noteHi.usage: संज्ञा, -ing या that-वाक्य के साथ; expect से अधिक औपचारिक।

noteJa.exampleTr: 劇場は初日の夜に大勢の観客を見込んでいる。
noteJa.meaning: 何かが起こると予期する。
noteJa.usage: 名詞・動名詞・that 節を続ける。expect より改まった語。

noteKo.exampleTr: 극장은 개막일 밤에 많은 관객을 예상하고 있다.
noteKo.usage: 명사, 동명사, that절이 뒤따르며 expect보다 격식 있다.

approximately.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the meeting.

arts.en: music, theatre, painting and similar activities
arts.ex: The city gives money to the arts every year.

as.en: in the same way; in the role of

asking.en: asking price: the price a seller wants
asking.ex: They paid less than the asking price for the flat.

assembly.en: assembly hall: a big room for meetings
assembly.ex: The students met in the assembly hall.

at.zh: 在（at the moment / at present：目前）

backing.ex: The festival has financial backing from the city.

base.en: the main place where a group works
base.ex: The team uses the old school as its base.

be.en: exist or have a quality; used to form the passive
be.ex: The shop will be open tomorrow.

become.ex: The empty lot will become a playground.

bidders.en: people who offer money to buy something
bidders.ex: Three bidders wanted the old hotel.

big.ex: The school has a big hall for concerts.

bodies.ex: Several public bodies support the plan.

bought.ex: We bought fresh bread this morning.

building.en: a structure with walls and a roof
building.ex: The old building has a red roof.

came.ex: The idea came from a student.

capital.en: the city where a country's government is
capital.ex: Tainan was once the capital of Taiwan.

capitals.en: main cities where countries are governed
capitals.ex: Paris and Rome are popular European capitals.

cavernous.ex: They held the party in a cavernous old barn.

changed.ex: They changed the kitchen to make it bigger.

changes.en: things done to make something different
changes.ex: We made a few changes to the garden.

chapel.en: a small church or a room for prayer
chapel.ex: The wedding took place in a small chapel.

church.ex: They got married in a small church.

city.ex: Tainan is an old city in Taiwan.

close.ex: Our hotel is close to the beach.

commercial.ex: The area has many commercial buildings.

company.en: a group of performers working together
company.ex: She joined a dance company in London.

consequently.ex: It rained heavily; consequently, the match was cancelled.

contribute.en: to give money to help pay
contribute.ex: Every parent will contribute ten euros to the trip.

converted.en: changed to be used for something else
converted.ex: The old barn was converted into a house.

cost.en: to need a certain amount of money
cost.ex: The new roof will cost a lot of money.

council.en: a group that runs a city
council.ex: The council plans to build a new library.

culture.ex: The city spends more money on culture now.

currently.ex: She is currently living in Cork.

dame.en: part of a street name in Dublin

dates.en: dates from: was first made at that time
dates.ex: The bridge dates from the Roman period.

dating.en: dating from: first made at that time
dating.ex: The castle dates from the twelfth century.

day.en: one day: at some time in the future
day.ex: One day I want to live by the sea.

dedicated.ex: The park has a dedicated lane for joggers.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: He works in the health department.

deterred.en: made someone not want to do something
deterred.ex: The high price deterred many visitors.

directly.ex: The bank is directly opposite the station.

director.en: the person who runs an organisation
director.ex: The director of the museum gave a short speech.

do.en: make do: manage with something not ideal
do.ex: We had no sofa, so we made do with chairs.

donors.en: people who give money to help
donors.ex: Local donors paid for the new playground.

downstairs.ex: The downstairs room is used as a kitchen.

earmarked.en: set aside for a particular purpose
earmarked.ex: The money was earmarked for building new schools.
earmarked.ja: 〜に充てられた；〜用に指定された

example.en: The money is earmarked for new musical instruments.
example.zh: 這筆錢已指定用於購買新樂器。

note.meaning: 指定、撥作（某特定用途），常指資金或空間。
note.usage: 常用被動 be earmarked for + 用途；也可 earmark A for B。

noteEn.meaning: to keep something, like money or space, for one purpose.
noteEn.usage: Usually passive: be earmarked for something.

noteEs.exampleTr: El dinero está destinado a nuevos instrumentos musicales.
noteEs.meaning: reservar algo, como dinero o un espacio, para un uso concreto.
noteEs.usage: Suele usarse en pasiva: be earmarked for.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह पैसा नए वाद्ययंत्रों के लिए तय किया गया है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी विशेष काम के लिए तय करना, ख़ासकर धन या जगह।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर be earmarked for + उद्देश्य के रूप में।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのお金は新しい楽器の購入に充てられている。
noteJa.meaning: お金や場所などを特定の用途に充てる。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be earmarked for が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 돈은 새 악기 구입용으로 배정되어 있다.
noteKo.usage: 수동태 be earmarked for 형태가 흔하다.

establishing.en: officially setting up or creating something
establishing.ex: They plan on establishing a music school in town.

estimated.ex: The trip is estimated to take four hours.

executive.en: having the power to manage things
executive.ex: She has an executive role in the bank.

expected.ex: The new park is expected to open in May.
expected.ja: 予想された；見込まれる

example.en: The city cut its expenditure on new buildings.
example.zh: 市政府削減了新建築的支出。

note.meaning: 支出、開支：花費的金錢總額，尤指政府或機構。
note.usage: 正式用語，常見 public expenditure、expenditure on + 項目。

noteEn.meaning: the money that is spent, often by a government.
noteEn.usage: Formal; common in public expenditure and expenditure on something.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad redujo su gasto en nuevos edificios.
noteEs.meaning: dinero total que se gasta, sobre todo un gobierno.
noteEs.usage: Formal; común en public expenditure, expenditure on.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने नई इमारतों पर अपना व्यय घटा दिया।
noteHi.meaning: ख़र्च की गई कुल राशि, ख़ासकर सरकार द्वारा।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक; public expenditure, expenditure on आम हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市は新しい建物への支出を削減した。
noteJa.meaning: 使われるお金の総額。特に政府や組織の支出。
noteJa.usage: 改まった語。public expenditure, expenditure on の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 새 건물에 대한 지출을 줄였다.
noteKo.meaning: 쓴 돈의 총액, 특히 정부나 기관의 지출.
noteKo.usage: 격식체이며 public expenditure, expenditure on으로 자주 쓰인다.

facing.ex: Our flat is facing the park.

financed.ex: The library was financed by a local bank.

find.en: to discover or get something you need
find.ex: I cannot find my keys anywhere.

fine.ex: The hall is known for its fine paintings.

first.en: coming before all others; for the first time, or at the beginning
first.ex: This is the first time I have visited Japan.

fixing.ex: He spent the day fixing the roof.

fledged.ex: After years of training, she is a fully fledged doctor.

foothold.en: a safe position to grow from
foothold.ex: The shop gained a foothold in the city market.

example.en: The small company gained a foothold in Asia.
example.zh: 這家小公司在亞洲站穩了腳步。

note.meaning: 立足點、據點：可在其上進一步發展的穩固位置。
note.usage: 常用 gain / secure / establish a foothold in + 地方或市場。

noteEn.meaning: a secure position from which you can grow.
noteEn.usage: Common in gain or secure a foothold in a place.

noteEs.exampleTr: La pequeña empresa consiguió afianzarse en Asia.
noteEs.meaning: posición segura desde la que se puede crecer.
noteEs.usage: Común en gain/secure a foothold in.

noteHi.exampleTr: छोटी कंपनी ने एशिया में पैर जमा लिए।
noteHi.meaning: एक मज़बूत शुरुआती स्थिति जहाँ से आगे बढ़ा जा सके।
noteHi.usage: gain/secure a foothold in के रूप में आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その小さな会社はアジアに足場を築いた。
noteJa.meaning: そこから発展できる確かな足場。
noteJa.usage: gain / secure a foothold in の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 작은 회사는 아시아에 발판을 마련했다.
noteKo.meaning: 더 성장할 수 있는 안정된 발판.
noteKo.usage: gain/secure a foothold in 형태로 자주 쓰인다.

form.en: the shape or look of something
form.ex: The old mill was rebuilt in its original form.

former.en: having been something in the past
former.ex: Kyoto is the former capital of Japan.

four-storey.ex: They live in a four-storey house near the river.

fully.ex: The hotel is fully booked this weekend.

function.en: to work or be used as something
function.ex: The garage will function as a music room.

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is central.

gave.ex: A local family gave money for the new park.

generosity.en: being happy to give money or help
generosity.ex: We thank our neighbours for their generosity.

getting.ex: The school is getting a new gym.

gift.en: gift shop: a shop selling presents
gift.ex: I bought a gift for my mother.

government.en: the group that runs a country

groups.en: organisations of people with shared interests
groups.ex: Several community groups joined the protest.

guide.en: guide price: the expected selling price
guide.ex: The guide price for the house is quite low.

hall.en: a large room for meetings or events
hall.ex: The concert takes place in the town hall.

hard.ex: It is hard to wake up early in winter.

has.en: owns or holds; also forms perfect tense

have.ex: Every room should have a window.

having.en: form of have before a past participle
having.ex: Having finished dinner, we went for a walk.

help.ex: The city may help pay for the new stage.

home.en: the place where a group is based
home.ex: The museum found a new home in the old station.

hopes.ex: The band hopes to play in Dublin.

host.en: to be the place where an event happens
host.ex: The school will host the music competition.

hotel.en: a building where people pay to stay
hotel.ex: We stayed in a hotel near the beach.

house.en: in opera house: a theatre for opera
house.ex: The new opera house opened last spring.

how.ex: She showed me how the machine works.

initial.ex: The initial plan was too expensive.

ino.ja: INO（アイルランド国立歌劇団）
ino.zh: INO（愛爾蘭國家歌劇院簡稱）

interest.en: wanting to buy or do something
interest.ex: There was little interest in the old factory.

into.en: to the inside of; changing to become something

involve.ex: The job involves a lot of travel.

just.ex: Just over half the class passed.

lacks.ex: The town lacks a good public library.

large.ex: The theatre needs a large stage.

large-scale.en: involving many people, things or a large area
large-scale.ex: The city has started a large-scale cleaning project.

likely.ex: It is likely to rain this afternoon.

limited.ex: Bad weather limited the number of visitors.

limits.en: rules about how much you can do
limits.ex: There are limits on how loud the music can be.

listed.ex: You cannot change the windows of a listed house.

main.ex: The main road is closed today.

making.en: making do: managing with something not ideal
making.ex: They are making do with one small car.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

may.ex: Kids may start school at four.
may.ja: …かもしれない；…することがある

moment.ex: I am busy at the moment.

money.ex: They saved money for a new car.

municipal.en: of a city or town government
municipal.ex: The municipal library is open on Sundays.

national.ex: The national team won the match.

need.ex: Big plays need a lot of actors.

notes.ex: The teacher notes that the class has improved.

now.ex: Right now we are living in a small flat.

o'connell.en: part of a main street name in Dublin
o'connell.zh: O'Connell Street：奧康諾街（都柏林主街）

off.en: near; just to the side of

offices.en: buildings or rooms where people work
offices.ex: The company moved to new offices.

old.en: having existed for a long time; of advanced age (old age)
old.ex: The old bridge will be closed next month.

on.en: used for a street; also in on the scale of
on.zh: 在（某街道）上；on the scale of：規模如

opera.en: a play where the words are sung
opera.ex: We went to the opera last Saturday.

operas.en: plays where the words are sung

orchestra.ex: My sister plays violin in the school orchestra.

orchestral.ex: The film has beautiful orchestral music.

other.ex: Other students joined the club later.

out.en: used in point out: to tell a fact
out.ex: She pointed out that the shop was closed.

paid.ex: We paid twenty euros for the tickets.

people.ex: Many people visit the market on Sundays.

performers.en: people who sing, act or play for an audience
performers.ex: The performers bowed at the end of the show.

permanent.en: lasting for a long time or always
permanent.ex: The museum has a permanent home at last.

philanthropists.en: rich people who give money to help others
philanthropists.ex: A local philanthropist paid for the new hospital wing.

example.en: A wealthy philanthropist paid for the new children's library.
example.zh: 一位富有的慈善家出資興建了新的兒童圖書館。

note.meaning: 慈善家：捐出大筆金錢幫助他人或支持公益、藝術的富人。
note.usage: 可數名詞；形容詞 philanthropic、名詞 philanthropy（慈善事業）。

noteEn.meaning: a rich person who gives a lot of money to help others.
noteEn.usage: A countable noun; related words are philanthropic and philanthropy.

noteEs.exampleTr: Un rico filántropo pagó la nueva biblioteca infantil.
noteEs.meaning: persona rica que da mucho dinero para ayudar a otros.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo contable; adjetivo philanthropic, sustantivo philanthropy.

noteHi.exampleTr: एक धनी परोपकारी ने बच्चों के नए पुस्तकालय का खर्च उठाया।
noteHi.meaning: अमीर व्यक्ति जो दूसरों की मदद के लिए बड़ा दान देता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 裕福な慈善家が新しい子ども図書館の費用を出した。
noteJa.meaning: 多額の寄付で社会や芸術を支える裕福な人。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。形容詞は philanthropic、名詞 philanthropy は「慈善活動」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 한 부유한 자선가가 새 어린이 도서관 비용을 댔다.
noteKo.meaning: 남을 돕기 위해 큰돈을 기부하는 부유한 사람.
noteKo.usage: 가산 명사이며 형용사 philanthropic, 명사 philanthropy도 있다.

pointing.en: pointing out: telling people a fact
pointing.ex: He left early, pointing out that he had work.

practise.en: to do something again and again to improve
practise.ex: The band practises every Tuesday night.

present.ex: The present building was finished in 1990.

price.ex: The price of the flat was too high for us.

principal.ex: Rice is the principal food in the region.

private.ex: The park was paid for by a private family.

production.en: a show put on in a theatre
production.ex: The school production of the musical was great.

productions.en: shows put on in a theatre
productions.ex: The theatre puts on five productions a year.

project.en: a large planned piece of work
project.ex: The bridge project will take five years.

proposals.ex: The council will discuss the proposals next week.

protected.en: kept safe by law from changes
protected.ex: The old bridge is a protected structure.

public.en: of or run by the government
public.ex: Public money paid for the new hospital.

purchasing.ex: They are purchasing a small house in the country.

readily.ex: Fresh fish is readily available here.

real.ex: The town finally has a real cinema.

redbrick.ex: We live in a redbrick house near the park.

refashioned.en: changed into a new shape or style
refashioned.ex: The old shop was refashioned into a café.

refurbishment.en: work to make a building like new
refurbishment.ex: The hotel is closed for refurbishment.

regards.en: thinks of something in a certain way
regards.ex: Many people regard him as a hero.

region.ex: The car cost in the region of ten thousand pounds.

rehearsal.ex: The last rehearsal ended very late.

rehearsals.ex: The choir has rehearsals every evening.

rehearse.ex: The actors rehearse in an old school hall.

rehearsing.ex: The band is rehearsing for the concert.
rehearsing.ja: リハーサルをしている

remains.ex: The museum remains the most visited place in town.

remodelled.ex: The old station was remodelled as a museum.

renovation.en: work to repair an old building
renovation.ex: The renovation of the castle took ten years.

paragraphs: Irish National Opera (INO) has bought an old church in Dublin. It is on Abbey Street, near O'Connell Street. The building is more than 200 years old.
INO paid €2.5 million for it. Private donors gave the money. Fixing the building will cost about €9 million more.
Right now, INO rents small offices above shops. INO will use the big rooms to practise. Some operas need 60 to 80 people in one room. There are not many rooms like this in Dublin.
The work could take two or three years. INO also wants Dublin to have a real opera house one day. It is a big step for INO.

Irish National Opera (INO) is getting its first permanent home. The company has bought a former Methodist church on Abbey Street in Dublin, just off O'Connell Street and almost opposite the Abbey Theatre.

INO paid €2.5 million for the building, and the money came from private donors. The church was built in 1820 and changed in 1901. It is a protected building, so there are limits on how it can be changed. Repairs and changes will cost about €9 million, and INO hopes the Government and Dublin City Council will help.

At the moment, INO rents offices above two gift shops on Dame Street. Big operas such as Carmen can have 60 to 80 people rehearsing in one room, and large spaces with good sound are hard to find in Dublin.

The old chapel will be used by the orchestra, and the upstairs hall will be the main rehearsal room. Building work could take two to three years. INO says this is a first step towards a real opera house for Dublin.
Irish National Opera (INO) has acquired its first permanent base: a former Methodist church on Abbey Street in Dublin, just off O'Connell Street and almost directly across from the Abbey Theatre.

The company paid €2.5 million, below the asking price of €2.75 million, with the money provided by private philanthropists. Built in 1820 and remodelled in 1901, the four-storey redbrick building is a protected structure, which limited interest from commercial buyers. Renovation is expected to cost around €9 million, and INO hopes to secure support from the Department of Culture and Dublin City Council.

INO currently rents offices above two gift shops on Dame Street. Its executive director, Diego Fasciati, says rehearsing a large production such as Carmen can involve 60 to 80 people in one room, and spaces with good acoustics are scarce in the city.
The downstairs chapel will become a rehearsal space for the orchestra, while the upstairs hall will be used for opera rehearsals. Other arts groups have also shown interest in using the rooms.
Works could take two to three years. INO sees the building as a first step towards a dedicated opera house, pointing out that Dublin is one of very few European capitals without one.

After years of making do with rented offices, Irish National Opera (INO) has secured a permanent foothold in the capital, purchasing a former Methodist church on Abbey Street, a stone's throw from O'Connell Street and almost facing the Abbey Theatre.

The company snapped up the building for €2.5 million, undercutting the €2.75 million guide price, thanks to the generosity of private philanthropists. Dating from 1820 and refashioned in 1901 into its present four-storey redbrick form, the listed structure deterred commercial bidders, since it could not readily be converted into, say, a hotel. Its refurbishment is projected to cost in the region of €9 million, for which INO is seeking state and municipal backing.

Executive director Diego Fasciati notes that staging a work on the scale of Carmen may require 60 to 80 performers to rehearse together, and that cavernous rooms with fine acoustics are in short supply in Dublin.

The chapel is earmarked for orchestral rehearsals, while the assembly hall upstairs will host opera rehearsals. Works are likely to span two to three years, and the company regards the venture as a stepping stone towards a fully fledged opera house, an amenity that Dublin, unlike most European capitals, still lacks.

Irish National Opera (INO) has acquired a permanent base for the first time, having purchased a former Methodist church on Abbey Street in Dublin, which is situated close to O'Connell Street and almost opposite the Abbey Theatre.

The acquisition cost €2.5 million, which was below the guide price of €2.75 million, and it was financed by private philanthropists. The building, which dates from 1820 and was substantially remodelled in 1901, is a protected structure; consequently, commercial interest was limited. Its renovation is estimated to require approximately €9 million, and INO anticipates that public bodies will contribute to this expenditure.

At present, the company rents offices above two gift shops on Dame Street. According to its executive director, Diego Fasciati, large-scale productions such as Carmen may involve 60 to 80 people rehearsing simultaneously, and suitable spaces with adequate acoustics are scarce in Dublin.

Under the proposals, the chapel will accommodate orchestral rehearsals, whereas the upstairs hall will function as the principal opera rehearsal space. The works are expected to take two to three years. Furthermore, INO regards the project as an initial step towards establishing a dedicated opera house, since Dublin remains one of very few European capitals without one.
